proposal.hypothesis: Compared with the selected weight-only hybrid (0.3058 s) and the measured full-state array-of-struct candidate (0.1790 s), this candidate retains per-axis cell, fraction, and smooth-weight reuse plus shared z state, but stores cells as bytes and state as separate arrays. The smaller nominal cache footprint may reduce scratch traffic; six vector allocations and separate array accesses may instead outweigh that benefit. No speedup is assumed.

retained: Keep the per-axis, per-octave full state: lattice cell, fraction, and smooth weight for x and y, plus per-octave z state and amplitude.

Represent x/y cells as unsigned bytes and fractions/weights as separate float arrays instead of padded integer/float state structs; include all six vector allocations and state accesses in the measured routine.
Preserve x0 + i * dx and y0 + j * dy before scaling, the lambda/amplitude progression, gradient and interpolation order, octave accumulation order, and output layout.
